Why do we encrypt, and in which three places?

Encryption protects confidentiality even if access (network, storage, administrator) is compromised, because without the key the data is unusable. You encrypt in transit with TLS to prevent a MITM attack, at rest on the server side with a key managed via KMS, and client side when the server must never be able to read the data. Example: HTTPS to an ALB, SSE-KMS on S3 and the Encryption SDK for a sensitive field.

What is the difference between symmetric and asymmetric encryption?

Symmetric uses a single key to encrypt and decrypt; it is fast and used for large volumes (AES-256). Asymmetric uses a public/private pair: you encrypt with the public key and decrypt with the private key, or sign with the private key and verify with the public key. TLS combines both: asymmetric to agree on a secret, then symmetric to encrypt the data.
